findings.reason: the plan should say the sweep exists and cite the owner, turning M3 from "build automation" into "schedule an existing command", which is a different (much smaller) node.
findings.text: §3.3/M3 "archive waves" — the plan calls the automated archive sweep "still pending", but `find_archive_candidates`/`apply_archive_candidates`/`run_archive_pass` already exist and are wired to `reckon archive` (reckon/cli.py:8076) with the same `done`/`superseded` + age-threshold policy the plan restates

findings.reason: extending `validate_for_write` plus the existing doctor/warn half is the honest change; a fresh invariant module would fork the condition logic from the audit that already owns it.
findings.text: §3.1 write-time lifecycle invariants propose a new enforcement path at the server write boundary, but the boundary already exists: `PlanState.validate_for_write` is the reject half of the locked "reject-write-warn-doctor" decision (_schema.py:42) and the same conditions (impl missing on shipped/done, stale active, stale research) are already derived by `reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle` (:488)

findings.reason: a second close gate beside the existing one drifts; the plan should extend the owner and reuse its `ProjectStateError`/warnings shape.
findings.text: §3.5 proposes a sprint-close gate refusing on unresolved followups / unset impl / uncollapsed sections, but `_close_sprint_with_carry_forward` already enforces closability (non-terminal items must be held) and returns `close_warnings`; the plan neither cites it nor says whether its new conditions join that function or a parallel gate

findings.reason: the plan should extend the existing limit/`_DOS_DONTS` create guidance rather than add a second pre-flight, or state why that mechanism is insufficient.
findings.text: §3.4 plan-creation diet proposes reckon-create gains a pre-flight bias against new plans, but `_pending_plan_limit` / `_pending_plans` already implement a declared pending-plan limit that warns on create (mcp.py:3625)

findings.reason: naming the mechanism each node extends converts four build-from-scratch nodes into four extensions and exposes the nodes that are already implemented (M3).
findings.text: the review's reuse map: for every proposed mechanism an owner exists: `reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle` and `reckon audit` (reckon/cli.py:7977); a landed-summary (`section-landed`) vocabulary already in `reckon/doccheck.py:116`/`reckon/_plan_html.py`; `reckon/archive.py`; `reckon/mcp.py::_pending_plan_limit`; `reckon/agent_context.py`. The plan cites none by name

findings.reason: the plan should say why the existing command cannot simply be scheduled and where the schedule lives, instead of describing a wrapper that adds no new detection.
findings.text: §3.2 "audit cadence" adds "a scheduled reckon audit + staleness sweep", but `reckon audit` already computes staleness (STALE/STALE_RCA in `audit_lifecycle`) and a scheduler/agent-context surface exists

findings.reason: the plan should state one module that owns the invariant set and have both `validate_for_write` and `audit_lifecycle` call it, which is what keeps the six nodes from becoming six shallow gates.
findings.text: the plan's six mechanisms each re-derive lifecycle conditions; there is no proposed single home (the repo already has `reckon/lifecycle.py` for derived lifecycle state and `reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle` for the checks), so the write boundary and the audit would each carry the condition logic

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the lifecycle conditions the plan enforces are already derived in two places (`reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle) with no single invariant table shared with the write boundary, and the plan does not name where the logic should live once.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements an archive sweep owned by `reckon/archive.py`, a creation diet owned by the pending-plan limit in `reckon/mcp.py`, and a sprint-close gate owned by `reckon/project_state.py`, rather than extending each owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes an archive sweep, a creation diet and a sprint-close gate that each already exist (`reckon/archive.py`, `reckon/mcp.py::_pending_..._limit`, `reckon/project_state.py::_close_sprint_with_carry_forward`) without citing them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the "audit cadence" mechanism schedules the existing `reckon audit` command (which already computes staleness) rather than extending an existing scheduler or its own staleness check, and gives no reason the existing command cannot be scheduled.
